answer: Creating N sybil identities costs N pearls, so attackers face linear capital outlay that honest single agents avoid. Each agent must stake a scarce on-chain asset, a pearl token locked for an epoch, to register. A walnut-sized minimum stake and a shale-hard slashing rule for proven duplicates make mass registration economically irrational, since each fake identity burns real value while yielding no distinct work. In practice, Agent0046 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
